sections.h2: Choosing how to sell in Milwaukee
sections.html:
A Milwaukee owner has three ways out. Hire an agent, go it alone, or let a cash buyer purchase the building exactly as it is today. Which one fits depends on the house's condition, any orders the city has issued against it, and the date you need money in hand.

Milwaukee has 562,407 residents, and just 41.8 percent of its housing units are lived in by owners. Expect plenty of the properties on the market to be rentals, duplexes and investor-held buildings. Owner-occupied homes carried a median value of $184,000 over 2020 to 2024, so one big repair bill can eat a large part of the price.

sections.h2: Flats, duplexes and tenants in place
sections.html:
Older brick is common here, and many blocks are lined with Polish flats, which are two-family houses with one unit above the other. An owner may occupy the upper unit and rent the lower one. An heir may inherit a flat with tenants still inside. Either way, buyers will read the leases, so decide early whether the tenants stay.

Leases, rent rolls and city registration records should be in a folder before the first buyer calls. Cash buyers will purchase a duplex with tenants in it, or a house with open orders, without asking you to fix anything. Put every offer in writing, then subtract your mortgage payoff, city charges and closing costs to see what you would really receive.

Short-term guest stays are a separate matter. DNS administers the state tourist rooming house license for stays shorter than a month, and an owner ending that use files a surrender form.

Most local checks run through the Department of Neighborhood Services (DNS). The department urges a DNS title search with every Milwaukee real estate transaction. The search form reveals pending code violations, special charges and city programs tied to the property, and whoever buys inherits any violation that was never abated.

  • Property registration. DNS requires registration of commercial property and of residential property nobody owner-occupies. Owner-occupied one-family, two-family and condo units are generally exempt. Use the Seller Notification Form (DNS-8D) to tell DNS ownership has changed, and call (414) 286-8569 with questions.
  • Vacant buildings. Thirty days of vacancy triggers registration. The buyer registers within 30 days of purchase, and your job as seller is to tell the buyer clearly that this is required. Putting up a For Sale sign does not cancel the duty.
  • Estates. Probate property that sits vacant is exempt when the personal representative or executor lives in the seven-county area around Milwaukee.
  • Open orders. Violations are posted in the DNS Land Management System. Call the section that issued an order to ask about it.

Nothing is charged for the first six months of vacant building registration, and DNS lists fees for renewals after that.

sections.h2: What Wisconsin requires of the seller
sections.html:
Owners of buildings with one to four units fall under Wis. Stat. 709.02. You fill out the real estate condition report, and the buyer needs it within 10 days of your accepting the contract. If it is late, the buyer gets two more business days to cancel. A court-appointed fiduciary who never lived in the house is excused, which is common in estate sales.

Under Wis. Stat. 77.22 the grantor, meaning you, pays 30 cents of transfer fee per $100 of value. Section 77.25 lists exemptions, such as a transfer by will or one between parent and child for nominal consideration. The return is filed online with the Department of Revenue. The register of deeds then takes the fee at recording.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Milwaukee County
sections.html:
Recording happens at the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds, 901 N. 9th Street, Room 103. Expect $30 per document, however many pages it runs, with the transfer fee from your e-RETR receipt on top. Pay in cash, by check or by money order. Cards are not taken.

  1. A title company or attorney drafts the deed. Register staff cannot write or review one for you.
  2. Submit the electronic return to the Department of Revenue and print your receipt.
  3. Deliver or mail the original deed, receipt and payment.

Documents are recorded as they arrive, within three to five business days, and the original is mailed to you one to two weeks later. The office phone is (414) 278-4005.

Revaluation of the whole city is typical every year at the Milwaukee Assessor's Office. Open Book takes place in the spring, and the assessor's website carries the next schedule. Look up any parcel at assessments.milwaukee.gov or phone the assessor at (414) 286-6565.

Property tax timeline for Milwaukee owners
StepTimingWhat happens
Assessment dateJanuary 1Value reflects market value as of that date
Bills mailedBy the third Monday in DecemberClerks send the bill
First installmentJanuary 31Unpaid balance turns fully delinquent on February 1
Second installmentJuly 31Last payment for installment payers

Delinquent tax collects interest at 1 percent a month. At closing, the title company divides the current year's bill between you and the buyer, so ask how that split will be handled.

sections.h2: Steps from first call to closing
sections.html:
Taking things in this sequence keeps surprises small.

  1. Order the DNS title search so no open violation or special charge surprises you.
  2. Settle whether the building counts as vacant and, if so, whether an exemption fits.
  3. With tenants in the building, collect leases, rent rolls and registration records.
  4. Request the payoff figure from your lender.
  5. Have every buyer write down a closing date and the fees that would come out of your proceeds.
  6. Fill in the condition report the moment a contract is signed. Ten days goes quickly.
  7. File the transfer return, then record the deed.
  8. Before closing, ask the title company which tax and utility balances need to be paid off.

Choosing a cash sale removes showings and buyer financing from the list. You still owe the report, the return and the recording.

Heirs often sell Milwaukee flats they did not choose to own. Three rules matter most. A personal representative or executor who lives within the seven-county area around Milwaukee can leave a vacant probate property off the vacancy registration list. A court-appointed fiduciary who never lived there does not have to complete the condition report. And a transfer made by will carries no state transfer fee.

Before you set a timetable, confirm with the probate court or an attorney who holds authority to sign. A buyer's title company will ask the same question, and the deed needs the right signatures before the register accepts it. A cash buyer can often work around an unfinished basement or a roof that needs help, but nobody can work around missing authority.

faqs.q: Is a title search from the city mandatory?
faqs.a: The city urges one on every sale but does not make it a legal requirement. It lists open violations, special charges and registration duties, which helps you and the buyer.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for the state transfer fee?
faqs.a: You are, as the grantor, at 30 cents per $100 of value under Wis. Stat. 77.22. It is collected at recording, and a transfer by will owes nothing.

faqs.q: Must a vacant house be registered before I sell it?
faqs.a: Yes, after 30 days or more of vacancy unless an exemption fits. A listing does not excuse it, and the buyer registers within 30 days of closing.

faqs.q: How quickly does the county record a deed?
faqs.a: Within three to five business days, in the order documents arrive. The original comes back by mail in one to two weeks.

faqs.q: Do I owe a buyer a condition report?
faqs.a: On most one-to-four unit homes, yes, within 10 days after the contract is accepted. A fiduciary who never occupied the home is exempt under Wis. Stat. 709.01.
